title: Implement recovery strategies
question: Given a service disruption, choose a recovery strategy that matches business impact and recovery objectives, identify dependencies and alternate capabilities, and define how trust and service acceptance will be restored.
scenario: A payment service has a 30-minute RTO and near-zero RPO, but its recovery site lacks the same identity, network, and key-management dependencies.
focalRelation: The strategy is incomplete until dependencies and trust services are included.

nodes.label: Payment service objective
nodes.detail: Business-defined 30-minute RTO, near-zero RPO, maximum tolerable disruption, priority, and acceptance owner.

nodes.label: Replicated data
nodes.detail: Candidate recovery state whose currency, integrity, consistency, and independent recovery points must be tested.

nodes.label: Recovery compute
nodes.detail: Alternate processing capacity that can start components but cannot supply missing trust services.

nodes.label: Identity and key services
nodes.detail: Required trust dependencies for authentication, authorization, decryption, and secure operation.

nodes.label: Recovery team
nodes.detail: Staff, supplier, access, communication, and runbook capability needed to execute within objectives.

nodes.label: Business acceptance
nodes.detail: Decision that the restored service is usable, secure, reconciled, monitored, and fit for prioritized traffic.

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: A payment service has a 30-minute RTO and near-zero RPO, but its recovery site lacks the same identity, network, and key-management dependencies.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: RTO concerns how quickly service returns; RPO concerns the acceptable data-loss point; MTD expresses business tolerance.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: A replicated production site eliminates disaster-recovery planning. Replication can copy corruption, rely on unavailable dependencies, or fail under regional, provider, identity, or human disruption.

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: The strategy is incomplete until dependencies and trust services are included. Test replication, key access, identity, network paths, staffing, communications, and business acceptance; otherwise a technically available application may not be a usable or safe service.

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Given a service disruption, choose a recovery strategy that matches business impact and recovery objectives, identify dependencies and alternate capabilities, and define how trust and service acceptance will be restored. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

prediction.prompt: The recovery site has compute, but not the production identity, network, and key-management dependencies. Is the payment service recovered?

options.label: Yes; alternate compute meeting the RTO makes the service available.
options.feedback: Compute cannot authenticate users, decrypt data, route trusted traffic, or establish business acceptance by itself.

options.label: No; test data, trust dependencies, capacity, monitoring, and business acceptance
options.feedback: Correct. Component availability is only candidate recovery until required dependencies and acceptance gates pass.

options.label: Yes if the replicated data meets the RPO, even without identity or key services.
options.feedback: RPO addresses data loss tolerance. It does not prove trusted operation, capacity, monitoring, or usable service.

prediction.hint: Separate time and data objectives from the dependencies required for trusted use.

transfer.prompt: A cloud region fails while the provider's status page reports the application healthy in a secondary region.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: Changed fact: A cloud region fails while the provider's status page reports the application healthy in a secondary region. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: The strategy is incomplete until dependencies and trust services are included. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Verify identity, data consistency, keys, network paths, monitoring, dependencies, and business acceptance before declaring recovery complete.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: Changed fact: A cloud region fails while the provider's status page reports the application healthy in a secondary region. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: The strategy is incomplete until dependencies and trust services are included. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

options.label: Verify identity, data consistency, keys, network paths, monitoring, dependencies
options.feedback: Correct. Verify identity, data consistency, keys, network paths, monitoring, dependencies, and business acceptance before declaring recovery complete.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: A backup restore meets its data-loss target, but DNS, identity, and key-service dependencies were not exercised. What is proven?

options.label: The backup meets the data objective; end-to-end service recovery remains unproven
options.feedback: Correct. A good restore does not by itself establish application availability or trusted operation.

options.label: The recovery strategy passes because the restored files meet RPO
options.feedback: RPO evidence does not prove DNS, identity, keys, networking, or end-to-end service.

options.label: The backup has no value because every dependency was not included in the same test
options.feedback: The restore supplies valid evidence for data recovery, while the broader service claim remains limited.

retry.hint: Separate recovered data from the dependencies required to deliver a usable trusted service.

takeaway: The strategy is incomplete until dependencies and trust services are included.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

learningJob.plainExplanation: RTO describes return time, RPO the acceptable data-loss point, and MTD the business tolerance. A recovery strategy must include trust, people, network, key, capacity, communication, and acceptance dependencies rather than alternate compute alone.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A dependency-and-time comparison would show why compute plus data does not satisfy RTO/RPO when identity, keys, network, and acceptance are absent; the opening does not.
